stories.headline: Nvidia board meets on ousting Jensen Huang after second affair report; CFO Kress eyed as interim CEO

key_facts.fact: Nvidia's board met on Wednesday, Nov 11, to decide whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang, after the Wall Street Journal reported the board was preparing to force him out; no decision had been announced by Thursday morning.
key_facts.excerpt: The board met Wednesday to discuss Mr. Huang but has made no announcement about any decision regarding Nvidia's longtime leader.

key_facts.fact: The New York Times reported on Wednesday that Huang had a separate extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, who reports to him; this followed his admission of an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive US intelligence suspects of spying for China.
key_facts.excerpt: Huang's position became more tenuous late on Wednesday after it was reported by the New York Times that Huang had a separate extramarital affair with a company employee named Kimberly Powell.

key_facts.fact: Some board members favor naming CFO Colette Kress interim CEO, and the board has debated adding a chief operating officer alongside an interim chief; Nvidia briefed the White House on its planned meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's board has debated whether, as part of its potential replacement of Huang, to introduce a chief operating officer to serve alongside the interim chief executive, some of the people said.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia has tapped an outside search firm to find a successor; Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji is among those being considered, per Semafor citing Bloomberg and a source.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has tapped an outside search firm to find the company's next CEO, Bloomberg reported. One person being considered for the top job is Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji

key_facts.fact: Under Nvidia's bylaws Huang can be removed with or without cause by a majority of its 11 directors; Huang, 63, owns about 3.6% of the stock and has no obvious successor.
key_facts.excerpt: Under Nvidia's bylaws, Huang can be removed "with or without cause" by a majority vote of directors. Nvidia has 11 directors and considers all but Huang independent.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia shares fell more than 8% in after-hours trading after the WSJ report, hitting a 52-week low.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's stock fell more than 8% in after-hours trading, hitting a 52-week low.

key_facts.fact: Rivals gained: AMD closed up 7.3% and rose 4%+ pre-market, while Broadcom gained 4% and then 2.4% pre-market as Nvidia's board weighed ousting Huang.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD's shares rose 4%+ pre-market, after closing up 7.3%, and Broadcom gained 2.4% pre-market, following a 4% gain, as Nvidia's board weighs ousting Jensen Huang

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is due to report quarterly results on Nov 17; Polymarket put the odds of Huang resigning or being removed by year-end at 88%.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is due to report its quarterly results on November 17 ... Polymarket put the probability of Huang resigning or being removed by the end of the year at 88%.

stories.headline: Commerce readies rule on remote chip access as Chinese AI firms rush to rent Nvidia capacity abroad

key_facts.fact: The US Commerce Department is finalizing a long-awaited rule to stop Chinese AI firms from remotely accessing advanced AI chips through data centers in other countries, The Information reported.
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: the US Commerce Department is finalizing a semiconductor control update that would prevent remote access and chip smuggling into China via data centers

key_facts.fact: Chinese AI companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered capacity at data centers outside China; a major Chinese cloud provider has discussed internally locking in overseas capacity and smaller labs are approaching Southeast Asian compute-rental providers, Reuters reported on Nov 12 citing three people.
key_facts.excerpt: A major Chinese cloud provider has discussed internally whether to lock in overseas Nvidia chip capacity, while some companies have contacted data-centre operators about reserving it, the people said.

key_facts.fact: The firms fear the Huang scandal will give momentum to the Remote Access Security Act, which the House passed 369-22 in January and which awaits Senate action.
key_facts.excerpt: The House of Representatives passed the bill in January by a 369-22 vote, and it awaits Senate action.

key_facts.fact: Traders and intermediaries in China's grey market have started stockpiling restricted Nvidia chips in anticipation of tougher enforcement.
key_facts.excerpt: The prospect of tougher enforcement has also fuelled demand for restricted Nvidia AI chips in China's grey market, prompting traders and intermediaries to start stockpiling these processors

key_facts.fact: Alibaba shares fell as much as 7.1% in Hong Kong on Thursday, while Z.ai and MiniMax each lost 7% or more.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of Alibaba, Z.ai and MiniMax fell in Hong Kong on Thursday. Alibaba shed up to 7.1% at its low point, and the other two each lost 7% or more.

key_facts.fact: Megaspeed said on Thursday it had assisted inspectors from the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security and hired a US law firm to catalog its GPUs, rejecting claims it illegally sent chips to China.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said Thursday that it had assisted inspectors from the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security and engaged a U.S. law firm to catalog its graphics processing units.

key_facts.fact: A Baker McKenzie attorney told The Information that Commerce lacks statutory authority to regulate remote access under existing law, and Commerce is still consulting other agencies before finalizing the rule.
key_facts.excerpt: A Baker McKenzie attorney told The Information the department lacks that authority under existing statute ... Commerce is still consulting other agencies before the rule can be finalized

stories.headline: Axios: Lutnick stalled Trump-approved crackdown on Nvidia chip diversion to China three times

key_facts.fact: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has resisted restricting companies suspected of diverting Nvidia AI chips to China, even though Trump approved action at least three times this year, in May, August and on Nov 5, Axios reported on Nov 11.
key_facts.excerpt: On at least three separate occasions — in May, August, and Nov. 5 — Trump approved taking action against suspected diversions of Nvidia chips to China. But Lutnick and Commerce Undersecretary Jeffrey Kessler resisted pressure

key_facts.fact: In a Situation Room meeting, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Lutnick over why Megaspeed had not been added to the Entity List; Defense Secretary Hegseth, USTR Greer and Secretary of State Rubio sided with Bessent.
key_facts.excerpt: At a White House Situation Room meeting on Thursday after the midterm elections, Bessent pressed Lutnick on why Megaspeed had not been added to the Commerce Department's entity list, to which Lutnick responded he would "look into it."

key_facts.fact: Trump called Elon Musk before approving the crackdown; Musk backed the hawks while Lutnick warned it 'will start a trade war with China', then proposed developing 'options' after Trump said 'Let's get it done.'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump called tech advisor Elon Musk and agreed to move forward. Musk supported Rubio, Bessent, Greer and Hegseth's case to impose the controls while Lutnick warned it "will start a trade war with China."

key_facts.fact: The Commerce Department denied that the Bessent-Lutnick confrontation took place.
key_facts.excerpt: "This is false. Secretary Bessent and Secretary Lutnick had no such conversation," spokesperson Kristen Eichamer said.

key_facts.fact: The US has posted no additions to its Entity List since October 2025, the longest gap in more than a decade.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. has not posted any additions to its Entity List since October 2025, the longest stretch between new postings in more than a decade.

key_facts.fact: Senators Chris Coons and Elizabeth Warren on Wednesday asked Lutnick, Rubio and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller to preserve documents on Nvidia chip exports to China and on Huang and the suspected Chinese operative.
key_facts.excerpt: Sens. Chris Coons, D-Del., and Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., sent a letter to members of President Donald Trump's Cabinet on Wednesday asking them to preserve documents related to Nvidia's chip exports to China

stories.headline: SMIC posts record $3.19B Q3 revenue as profit more than doubles, guides margin lower

key_facts.fact: SMIC's Q3 2026 revenue was $3.19 billion, up 6.1% from Q2 and 33.9% year over year, driven by higher wafer shipments.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue was $3,190.0 million in 3Q26, compared to $3,005.6 million in 2Q26, and $2,381.8 million in 3Q25.

key_facts.fact: Profit attributable to owners rose 123.4% year over year to $428.4 million, though it fell 10.6% from Q2 as investment gains shrank.
Gross margin reached 29.9%, up from 25.3% in Q2 and above its 26%-28% guidance, on capacity utilization of 97.3% and product mix.
key_facts.excerpt: Gross margin increased to 29.9% from 25.3% and 22%, respectively, as plant utilisation improved to 97.3% from 93.7% in the previous quarter and product mix changed.

key_facts.fact: For Q4, SMIC guides revenue up 4%-6% sequentially with gross margin falling back to 26%-28%.
key_facts.excerpt: In the fourth quarter, the Company's revenue is expected to increase 4% to 6% sequentially, and the gross margin is expected to be in the range of 26% to 28%.

key_facts.fact: China accounted for 90.8% of revenue; monthly capacity rose 1.8% to 1.1 million 8-inch-equivalent wafers, and Q3 capex was $1.09 billion versus $1.84 billion in Q2; results beat LSEG estimates.
key_facts.excerpt: Kina förblev SMIC:s största marknad och stod för 90,8 procent av intäkterna ... SMIC:s investeringar under tredje kvartalet uppgick till 1,09 miljarder dollar, jämfört med 1,84 miljarder dollar under andra kvartalet.

stories.headline: Foxconn Q3 profit jumps 34% to a record on AI servers; sees strong AI rack growth in 2027

key_facts.fact: Foxconn's July-September net profit rose 34% to T$77.5 billion ($2.35 billion), beating the LSEG consensus of T$69.6 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Net profit for the July to September period for Nvidia's biggest server maker and Apple's top iPhone assembler was T$77.5 billion ($2.35 billion), up 34% on year and beating an LSEG consensus estimate of T$69.6 billion.

key_facts.fact: Q3 revenue rose 46% to NT$3.02 trillion, cloud and networking products reached 54% of sales, and operating income jumped 64% to NT$115.35 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Net profit attributable to shareholders rose 34% from a year earlier to NT$77.52 billion ... on revenue of NT$3.02 trillion, up 46% ... Operating income jumped 64% to NT$115.35 billion

key_facts.fact: Foxconn forecast 'high double-digit growth' in AI rack shipments in 2027, and Chairman Young Liu said cloud and networking should exceed 60% of revenue within three to five years.
key_facts.excerpt: The company, which does not give numeric forecasts, said it predicted "high double-digit growth" in 2027 for AI rack shipments.

key_facts.fact: Liu warned that chips, memory and some key components are tight and that demand is expected to exceed supply next year.
key_facts.excerpt: "Although supply bottlenecks should gradually ease as new capacity comes online, overall demand is expected to still exceed supply next year, and the tight supply-demand situation may persist for some time," he said.

key_facts.fact: Liu called AI servers Foxconn's most important growth driver; the company is building factories in Mexico and Texas to make AI servers for Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: "AI servers have become Foxconn's most important growth driver," Chairman Young Liu told a briefing.

stories.headline: SoftBank leads $500M round in German robot maker Agile Robots at $8.5B valuation

key_facts.fact: Munich-based Agile Robots raised $500 million in a round led by SoftBank, valuing it at $8.5 billion and bringing total funding to about $2 billion; Nvidia, Hitachi and T.Capital also took part.
key_facts.excerpt: The company raised $500 million, bringing the startup's total funding raised to about $2 billion, Munich-based Agile said in a statement. Nvidia Corp., Hitachi Ltd. and T.Capital also participated in the round.

key_facts.fact: The company builds robotic arms, hands, autonomous mobile robots and humanoids plus the software and AI models behind them, and was spun out of the German Aerospace Centre in 2018.
key_facts.excerpt: The Munich-based robotics company manufactures robotic arms, hands, autonomous mobile robots and humanoid robots, as well as building the software and AI models behind the tech.

key_facts.fact: Agile says it has deployed around 20,000 robots and opened a factory near Munich this year that can produce up to 10,000 humanoids annually.
key_facts.excerpt: The company says it has deployed around 20,000 robots in industries including automotive, consumer electronics and logistics. Earlier this year it opened a factory outside Munich that it says can produce up to 10,000 humanoid robots annually

key_facts.fact: Founder Zhaopeng Chen said the money funds US expansion and more German production ahead of a potential future IPO; the company works with partners including Google DeepMind.
key_facts.excerpt: The investment will allow Agile to expand in the United States, increase production in Germany and move into new markets — ahead of a potential future initial public offering, said Zhaopeng Chen, Agile's founder.

key_facts.fact: The valuation puts Agile ahead of German rival Neura Robotics (about $7 billion in June); talks in June had discussed a raise of around $800 million.
key_facts.excerpt: At $8.5 billion, Agile moves ahead of fellow German startup Neura Robotics, which reached a valuation of roughly $7 billion in June

stories.headline: CoreWeave plans at least $4B chip-backed investment-grade loan at about half its junk-bond yield

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave is preparing to raise at least $4 billion through an investment-grade loan led by Morgan Stanley and MUFG that could launch as early as next week, Bloomberg reported on Nov 11.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction, led by Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc., would be syndicated in phases and could launch as early as next week, though terms remain subject to change.

key_facts.fact: Early pricing points to a 7%-7.5% yield, roughly half the yield on its existing high-yield debt; its 9.625% notes due 2032 traded at a 14.21% yield on Nov 11.
key_facts.excerpt: Preliminary discussions put the new loan's yield at 7% to 7.5%, roughly half the yield on CoreWeave's existing junk bonds ... CoreWeave's 9.625% notes due July 2032 traded at a 14.21% yield on 11 November.

key_facts.fact: The junk-rated company is structuring the loan around its computing hardware and customer contracts, mirroring an $8.5 billion investment-grade facility backed by Meta contracts in March.
key_facts.excerpt: the junk-rated firm is structuring the facility around its computing hardware and underlying customer commitments, mirroring an $8.5 billion investment-grade transaction completed in March.

key_facts.fact: CEO Michael Intrator said CoreWeave will not use the unsecured debt market at current yields, and has cancelled his pre-arranged plans to sell company stock.
key_facts.excerpt: Chief Executive Michael Intrator told CNBC earlier in the day that he has canceled his pre-arranged plans to sell company stock ... "Looking ahead, we will not use the unsecured debt market to fund our business at current yields, nor do we need to,"
